The Future of LLMs and LLMOpsLLM 与 LLMOps 的未来

— 原书第 255 页 —

In the next decade, the future of LLMOps, LLMs, NLP, and knowledge graphs will converge in ways we can barely imagine today. Imagine AI systems no longer as distant tools but as deeply integrated into every facet of our lives. Even the most popular LLMs today are somewhat clunky iterations, but in the near future, I believe they will be refined to a point where their understanding of language will rival human intuition. This is because of emergent traits in LLMs.

在下一个十年里，LLMOps、LLM、NLP 和知识图的未来将以我们今天几乎难以想象的方式汇聚。想象一下，AI 系统不再是遥远的工具，而是深度融入我们生活的方方面面。即便今天最流行的 LLM 也仍有些笨拙，但在不久的将来，我相信它们会被打磨到语言理解能力可与人类直觉相媲美的程度。这源于 LLM 的涌现特性。

Currently, the main way users interact with LLMs is through text-based chats, but in coming years, LLMs won't just be answering questions; they'll be engaging in complex problem-solving, offering insights, and pushing the boundaries of creativity itself. For example, in September 2024, OpenAI released Advanced Voice Mode for its ChatGPT application, which can detect voice tone—including sarcasm. Much of this work is related to impending innovations across the infrastructure stack. Meta recently wrote about issues beyond algorithms and architecture that arise in training these models at scale (see Figure 10-1).

目前用户与 LLM 交互的主要方式是文本聊天，但在未来几年，LLM 不只是回答问题；它们还将参与复杂问题求解、提供洞见，并推动创造力本身的边界。例如，2024 年 9 月 OpenAI 为其 ChatGPT 应用发布了高级语音模式，能识别语气——包括讽刺。这些工作很大程度上与整个基础设施栈即将到来的创新相关。Meta 最近撰文谈到在大规模训练这些模型时，算法和架构之外出现的种种问题（见图 10-1）。

LLMOps will be the backbone supporting these systems as they mature into a seamless, self-sustaining infrastructure. Instead of manual intervention, pipelines for training, fine-tuning, and deploying these models will be fully automated, speeding up advances in this area. LLMOps engineers will spend less time debugging code and more time refining high-level system strategies, including platform and infrastructure designs that automatically balance model training with compute costs.

当这些系统成熟为无缝、自维持的基础设施时，LLMOps 将是支撑它们的骨干。训练、微调和部署这些模型的流水线将不再需要人工干预，而是完全自动化，从而加快该领域的进步。LLMOps 工程师将花更少时间调试代码，而花更多时间打磨高层系统策略，包括自动平衡模型训练与算力成本的平台和基础设施设计。

— 原书第 256 页 —

These models will adapt on the fly, learning from real-world feedback at a rate that feels almost magical. This has been the primary goal of AutoML, which is an active area of research in ML. Most importantly, as LLMs start generating higher-quality translated content, they can more easily expand their capabilities to additional languages, even less common ones. An additional source of excitement (Figure 10-2) is that LLMs are getting better at using multimodal inputs. Currently, it takes an LLM a few seconds to process text, voice, and images, and a lot of progress is being made in simultaneous speech-to-text translation, a critical step toward speech-to-speech translation. Once simultaneous speech-to-text quality is high enough, existing text-to-speech models such as OpenAI Whisper can be used to complete the speech-to-speech translation pipeline.

这些模型将即时适应，以一种近乎神奇的速度从真实反馈中学习。这一直是 AutoML 的主要目标——AutoML 是 ML 中活跃的研究领域。最重要的是，随着 LLM 开始生成更高质量的翻译内容，它们可以更容易地把能力扩展到更多语言，哪怕是小语种。另一个令人兴奋之处（图 10-2）是 LLM 越来越擅长使用多模态输入。目前 LLM 处理文本、语音和图像需要几秒钟，而同步语音到文本翻译正在取得大量进展——这是迈向语音到语音翻译的关键一步。一旦同步语音到文本的质量足够高，就可以用 OpenAI Whisper 等现有文本到语音模型补全语音到语音翻译流水线。

— 原书第 257 页 —

One of the limitations of LLMs is that, at their core, they generate the most likely next word based on the data they were trained on and the prompt submitted, but they don't seem to understand even simple concepts. In a popular example (pictured in Figure 10-3), Meta's LLM could easily tell that Tom Cruise's mom is Mary Lee Pfeiffer but had trouble with the question “Who is Mary Lee Pfeiffer's famous actor son?” It frequently answered with the names of other famous actors, such as Matt Damon, Tom Hanks, and Michelle Pfeiffer—the “famous actor” part of the prompt took precedence.

LLM 的局限之一是：从核心上说，它们基于训练数据和所提交的提示生成最可能的下一个词，但似乎并不理解哪怕简单的概念。一个广为流传的例子（图 10-3）中，Meta 的 LLM 能轻易说出汤姆·克鲁斯的妈妈是 Mary Lee Pfeiffer，却在“Mary Lee Pfeiffer 那位著名的演员儿子是谁？”这个问题上卡壳。它频繁给出其他著名演员的名字，如马特·达蒙、汤姆·汉克斯和米歇尔·菲佛——提示中“著名演员”这部分占了上风。

One solution that is under research is to use knowledge graphs that contain relationships between concepts. Knowledge graphs contain representations of interconnected concepts and their relationships. For example, Wikipedia lists Mary Lee Pfeiffer as Tom Cruise's mother, but the fact that he is her son is not written down: it's implicit. Knowledge graphs make relationships explicit, creating systems that understand context in a way that's almost human.

一个正在研究中的解决方案是使用包含概念间关系的知识图。知识图包含相互关联的概念及其关系的表示。例如，维基百科把 Mary Lee Pfeiffer 列为汤姆·克鲁斯的母亲，但“他是她儿子”这一事实并没有被写下来：它是隐含的。知识图让关系变得显式，创造出以近乎人类的方式理解上下文的系统。

— 原书第 258 页 —

Conversations with LLMs will become indistinguishable from human conversations. No more fumbling with chatbots or dealing with “robotic” responses. Advances in personalization can allow future LLM applications to combine several facts they learn about users in the course of their interactions. Simple versions of this already exist today. For example, ChatGPT already learns what programming language an individual user frequently asks questions about and provides answers in that language by default. Recent research provides several other examples of adding personalization for education, healthcare, and finance. Although these use cases currently appear mostly in research papers, when deployed successfully in production across every ecommerce application out there, LLMs will anticipate users' needs, contextualize interactions, and even predict trends—all while learning continuously from new data streams.

与 LLM 的对话将变得与人类对话难以区分。不再需要笨拙地对付聊天机器人或处理“机器人式”回复。个性化方面的进步能让未来的 LLM 应用把交互过程中了解到的关于用户的若干事实组合起来。简单版本今天已经存在。例如，ChatGPT 已经能学习某个用户常问哪种编程语言的问题，并默认用那种语言回答。近来的研究还提供了在教育、医疗、金融中加入个性化的其他几个例子。尽管这些用例目前大多出现在论文中，但当它们成功部署到生产环境、铺遍每一个电商应用时，LLM 将预判用户需求、把交互置于语境中，甚至预测趋势——同时持续从新数据流中学习。

One of the key concerns people voice about LLMs has to do with the alignment risks associated with these models; namely, if a model is capable of showing emergence and can predict and emulate human behavior, then how do we know it will continue to be helpful in the long run? Should development pause while researchers closely monitor these models' performance? How can we ensure that the model is not behaving in a sociopathic way, providing harmless answers only when it realizes it's being tested? Researchers are exploring answers to these questions.

人们对 LLM 表达的一个主要担忧与这些模型的对齐风险有关；即如果一个模型能展现涌现能力、能预测和模仿人类行为，我们怎么知道它长期还会保持有用？是否应在研究人员密切监控这些模型表现期间暂停开发？我们如何确保模型不是在反社会式地行事——只在意识到自己被测试时才给出无害回答？研究者正在探索这些问题的答案。

As someone who believes in holding a Stoic outlook toward this future, my opinion is that we should embrace any technology that makes life simpler, richer, and more meaningful. As with all progress, the true winners will be those who understand that it's not about the machine but about how we, as humans, use it wisely.

作为一个对未来秉持斯多葛式态度的人，我的看法是：我们应拥抱任何让生活更简单、更丰富、更有意义的技术。如同所有进步一样，真正的赢家会明白：关键不在于机器本身，而在于我们人类如何明智地使用它。

LLM architecture has advanced exponentially from the mid-2010s to the mid-2020s, but the coming years promise even more profound shifts. These changes will redefine not only how LLMs are structured but also how they interact with data, humans, and each other. From increased scalability to more efficient computation, from hybrid architectures combining multiple paradigms to emergent self-learning systems, the future of LLMs has breathtaking potential. This chapter explores several aspects of that potential.

LLM 架构从 2010 年代中期到 2020 年代中期呈指数级进步，但未来几年必将带来更深刻的转变。这些变化不仅会重新定义 LLM 的结构，还会重新定义它们与数据、人类以及彼此交互的方式。从更强的可扩展性到更高效的计算，从结合多种范式的混合架构到涌现的自学习系统，LLM 的未来有着令人屏息的潜力。本章探讨这一潜力的几个方面。

Scaling Beyond Current Boundaries超越当前边界的扩缩

Today's LLMs, like GPT-4, have reached impressive scales, but they are far from their limits. Going into the 2030s, we should expect to see architectures designed with scalability in mind from the ground up. This is not simply about increasing the number of parameters; it's about efficient, targeted scaling. Future architectures will incorporate hierarchical layers of models (also known as hierarchical attention networks), where each layer is optimized for a specific domain of understanding such as reasoning, emotion, or even creativity (see Figure 10-4).

今天的 LLM，如 GPT-4，已达到令人印象深刻的规模，但远未触及极限。进入 2030 年代，我们应期待看到从一开始就把可扩展性纳入设计的架构。这不只是增加参数量，而是高效、有针对性的扩缩。未来架构将融入模型的层级化分层（也称分层注意力网络），每一层都针对特定理解领域优化，例如推理、情感甚至创造力（见图 10-4）。

— 原书第 259 页 —

Rather than creating ever-larger monolithic models, we'll see more modular LLMs that can delegate tasks to specialized submodels. Imagine an architecture where the base LLM understands language but calls on additional “expert” modules trained for niche tasks like legal reasoning, medical diagnostics, or creative writing. Instead of having one large base model trying to be an expert in everything, we would have models that are experts in different things: a healthcare model, a legal model, a creative writing model, etc.

我们不会看到一味制造更大的单体模型，而会看到更多模块化 LLM，能把任务委派给专用子模型。设想一种架构：基座 LLM 理解语言，但调用额外的“专家”模块——这些模块针对法律推理、医疗诊断或创意写作等小众任务训练。我们不会有一个大基座模型试图样样精通，而会有各有所专的模型：医疗模型、法律模型、创意写作模型等。

A specialist model can outperform a generalist model and use fewer resources. This is already happening for math problems and web searches in ChatGPT. Researchers have found that GPT performs below average in graduate-level math, and all GPT models have knowledge cutoffs, meaning that they are unaware of events after their cutoff date. Currently, when GPT detects that an user is asking a question about an event that occurred after its training cutoff date, it outsources the question to a different model called SearchGPT, then uses the results to provide an answer inside the existing chat. Combining generalist models with specialist models allows LLMs to operate efficiently and with greater depth in specialized areas, reducing the computational overhead while improving output precision.

专家模型可以胜过通用模型，且使用更少资源。这在 ChatGPT 的数学题和网页搜索中已经发生。研究发现 GPT 在研究生级数学上表现低于平均，而且所有 GPT 模型都有知识截止日期，意味着它们不知道截止日期之后的事件。目前，当 GPT 检测到用户在问一个训练截止日期之后发生的事件时，它会把问题外包给一个叫 SearchGPT 的不同模型，然后用结果在现有对话中给出回答。把通用模型与专家模型结合，让 LLM 既能高效运行，又能在专业领域有更深的造诣，在降低计算开销的同时提升输出精度。

— 原书第 260 页 —

To support such adaptable massive systems, innovations in distributed computing and parallelization will be key. As Evan Morikawa, who led OpenAI engineering when ChatGPT was becoming ever more popular, explains in an interview, models need to be hosted not on singular clusters but across decentralized networks of nodes. This shift will optimize training times, data latency, and real-time inference, making LLMs vastly more efficient in handling large-scale, real-world applications.

要支持这种可适应的巨型系统，分布式计算和并行化方面的创新将是关键。正如在 ChatGPT 日益火爆时领导 OpenAI 工程的 Evan Morikawa 在一次采访中解释的那样，模型不应托管在单一集群上，而应分布在去中心化的节点网络上。这一转变将优化训练时间、数据延迟和实时推理，让 LLM 在处理大规模真实应用时效率大幅提升。

Hybrid Architectures: Merging Neural Networks with Symbolic AI混合架构：融合神经网络与符号 AI

One of the current limitations of LLMs lies in their reliance on deep learning alone, which excels at pattern recognition but struggles with symbolic reasoning and logic. In many cases, scientists have already discovered patterns and codified them into symbolic formulas (e.g., Newton's theory of gravity), but the way neural networks are trained doesn't allow them to use existing formulas—they have to rediscover patterns by themselves.

LLM 当前的局限之一在于它们仅依赖深度学习，而深度学习擅长模式识别却不擅长符号推理和逻辑。在许多情况下，科学家早已发现模式并把它们编成符号公式（例如牛顿引力理论），但神经网络的训练方式不允许它们使用现成公式——它们必须自己重新发现模式。

The future of LLMs will involve hybrid architectures that merge the strengths of neural networks with symbolic AI approaches. These architectures will allow models not only to predict the next word in a sentence but also to use known rules and formulas, as humans do.

LLM 的未来将涉及融合神经网络与符号 AI 之长的混合架构。这些架构将让模型不仅能预测句子中的下一个词，还能像人类一样使用已知规则和公式。

Neurosymbolic, or “hybrid,” AI architectures unite the intuitive, pattern-matching power of neural networks with the precise, rule-based reasoning of symbolic systems. LLMs excel at processing text and generating natural-sounding responses by learning statistical regularities from massive datasets, while symbolic AI can represent explicit facts, logical constraints, and rules, making it far easier to trace its reasoning process and enforce consistency. By merging these two approaches, we will develop systems that can understand human language, perform rigorous logical operations, and provide explanations for their conclusions.

神经符号（或称“混合”）AI 架构把神经网络直觉式的模式匹配能力与符号系统精确的、基于规则的推理结合起来。LLM 通过从海量数据集中学习统计规律，擅长处理文本并生成自然流畅的回答；而符号 AI 能表示显式事实、逻辑约束和规则，使其推理过程更容易追溯、一致性更容易执行。融合这两种方式，我们将开发出能理解人类语言、执行严格逻辑运算、并为其结论提供解释的系统。

In practice, this can manifest in multiple ways. For instance, one method is to have an LLM convert user queries into structured representations—such as logical formulas—and then rely on a symbolic reasoner to apply domain-specific rules or constraints. This hybrid approach can also aid in explainability—one of the key weaknesses in today's LLMs. Users will be able to query why the model arrived at a particular conclusion, and the model can refer to the symbolic pathways used in the answer, providing a more transparent window into its decision-making process.

在实践中，这可以有多种表现。例如，一种方法是让 LLM 把用户查询转换成结构化表示——如逻辑公式——然后依靠符号推理器应用领域特定的规则或约束。这种混合方式还有助于可解释性——这是当今 LLM 的关键弱点之一。用户将能追问模型为何得出某个结论，模型可以引用回答中使用的符号路径，为其决策过程提供更透明的窗口。

— 原书第 261 页 —

Sparse and Mixture-of-Experts Models稀疏模型与混合专家模型

One of the biggest bottlenecks in scaling LLMs today is their sheer computational cost. Current models process every input with all their parameters, at inference time, regardless of the complexity or simplicity of the task. Future architectures will move toward sparse models and mixture-of-experts systems, where only a subset of the model's parameters is activated for a given task.

当今扩缩 LLM 最大的瓶颈之一是其高昂的计算成本。现有模型在推理时用全部参数处理每个输入，无论任务复杂还是简单。未来架构将走向稀疏模型和混合专家系统，即对给定任务只激活模型参数的一个子集。

In sparse models, only the most relevant parameters or neurons are activated for a particular query, allowing for massive reductions in resource consumption while maintaining high-quality results. We believe that sparse modeling, combined with the modular approach, will lead to the development of powerful, efficient LLMs capable of running on consumer-grade hardware while delivering enterprise-level performance.

在稀疏模型中，对特定查询只激活最相关的参数或神经元，从而在保持高质量结果的同时大幅降低资源消耗。我们相信，稀疏建模结合模块化方式，将催生强大而高效的 LLM，能在消费级硬件上运行，同时交付企业级性能。

Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, by contrast, allow LLMs to dynamically activate specialized “experts” based on the input's requirements. A user asking for medical advice would engage a different subset of the model's neurons than a user requesting help with poetry. This approach drastically reduces the number of computations per query while increasing the depth of understanding in each domain. It's a “divide and conquer” strategy, where LLMs focus computational resources only where they are needed most.

相比之下，混合专家（MoE）模型允许 LLM 根据输入需求动态激活专门的“专家”。寻求医疗建议的用户与请求诗歌帮助的用户，会激活模型神经元的不同子集。这种方式大幅减少每次查询的计算量，同时加深各领域的理解深度。这是一种“分而治之”策略，让 LLM 只在最需要的地方集中计算资源。

Memory-Augmented Models: Toward Persistent, Context-Rich AI记忆增强模型：迈向持久、上下文丰富的 AI

Current LLMs operate with limited memory. While capable of handling context within a few thousand tokens, they struggle to maintain long-term memory across sessions. The next generation of LLMs will address this with memory-augmented architectures capable of storing and retrieving vast amounts of data over long periods. These models will have persistent memory layers, allowing them to recall user interactions from years ago or build a comprehensive knowledge base that evolves with time.

当前 LLM 的内存有限。虽然能处理几千 token 内的上下文，但难以跨会话维持长期记忆。下一代 LLM 将用记忆增强架构解决这一问题，能够长期存储和检索海量数据。这些模型将拥有持久记忆层，能回忆起多年前的用户交互，或构建一个随时间演进的综合知识库。

This kind of persistent memory will also revolutionize how LLMs handle personalized tasks. Rather than starting from scratch with each interaction, future models will remember the user's preferences, needs, and history, enabling richer, more nuanced conversations and solutions. However, that comes with its own challenges in production, including unexpected behavior when dealing with inconsistencies in data. For example, imagine a single parent who is a senior government official but who also asks questions about how to raise a female child without specifically telling the model that the questions are about another person. For example, they ask, “What are the signs that my first period is arriving?” instead of “What are the signs that my daughter's first period is arriving?” The personalization algorithm may incorrectly conclude that the user is a teenage girl who is also a senior government official.

这种持久记忆也将彻底改变 LLM 处理个性化任务的方式。未来的模型不会每次交互都从零开始，而是记住用户的偏好、需求和历史，从而实现更丰富、更细致的对话和解决方案。然而这在生产中也带来自身挑战，包括处理数据不一致时的意外行为。例如，想象一位单亲家长是高级政府官员，却又问如何抚养女孩的问题，而没有明确告诉模型这些问题是关于另一个人的。例如他们问“我第一次来月经有什么征兆？”而不是“我女儿第一次来月经有什么征兆？”个性化算法可能错误地得出结论：用户是一个少女，同时又是高级政府官员。

— 原书第 262 页 —

Persistent memory will be key in enterprise applications, where models will continuously learn from organizational data, building an ever-growing repository of insights and expertise.

持久记忆在企业应用中将是关键——模型将持续从组织数据中学习，建立一个不断增长的洞见与专业知识仓库。

Interpretable and Self-Optimizing Models可解释与自优化模型

As LLMs become more pervasive, the need for interpretability will grow. Users and businesses alike will demand models that can explain their reasoning, mitigate biases, and adapt in real time. Future LLM architectures will include built-in interpretability features using causal learning, where each decision or prediction can be traced back through a chain of reasoning or probabilistic mapping.

随着 LLM 日益普及，对可解释性的需求将增长。用户和企业都将要求模型能解释其推理、缓解偏见并实时适应。未来 LLM 架构将内置使用因果学习的可解释性特性，每个决策或预测都能通过推理链或概率映射追溯回去。

These models will also be self-optimizing. Using reinforcement learning, LLMs will learn from user feedback, fine-tuning their own parameters to better align with desired outcomes. Over time, these models will become more personalized, adjusting not just to individuals but also to the specific needs of organizations or industries.

这些模型还将是自优化的。通过强化学习，LLM 将从用户反馈中学习，微调自身参数以更好地对齐预期结果。随着时间推移，这些模型将变得更个性化，不仅适应个人，还适应组织或行业的特定需求。

Imagine a legal AI model that, after interacting with a team of lawyers for months, begins to understand the specific nuances of that firm's legal style, approach to risk, and preferred legal precedents. These models will learn through iterative feedback, continuously improving without needing massive retraining efforts. They are currently being explored (Huang et al. 2022; Jin et al. 2025) as agents to aid operational productivity, but many applications remain unexplored.

设想一个法律 AI 模型，在与一个律师团队互动数月后，开始理解该律所法律风格、风险处理方式和偏好判例的具体微妙之处。这些模型将通过迭代反馈学习，持续改进而无需大规模重训。它们目前正被探索（Huang 等 2022；Jin 等 2025）作为辅助运营生产力的智能体，但许多应用仍待探索。

Cross-Model Collaboration, Meta-Learning, and Multi-Modal Fine-Tuning跨模型协作、元学习与多模态微调

In the future, no single LLM will operate in isolation. We'll see architectures where multiple models collaborate, exchanging data, insights, and strategies in real time. Meta-learning will also become more prominent, so instead of having to be trained from scratch, LLMs will learn how to learn. This means they will be capable of adjusting their architectures dynamically based on the tasks they encounter and will optimize themselves without human intervention, using different distillation techniques.

未来，没有哪个 LLM 会孤立运行。我们将看到多个模型协作的架构，实时交换数据、洞见和策略。元学习也将变得更加重要，LLM 不必从头训练，而将学会如何学习。这意味着它们能根据遇到的任务动态调整自己的架构，并使用不同的蒸馏技术在无人干预下自我优化。

This shift will push LLMs toward becoming self-evolving entities, reducing the need for constant retraining and manual updates. Overall, we will move beyond the brute-force scaling of today's models to more refined, hybridized architectures capable of reasoning, learning, and adapting in ways that feel almost human.

这一转变将推动 LLM 成为自演进实体，减少对持续重训和手动更新的需求。总体而言，我们将超越当今模型的暴力式扩缩，走向更精致、更混合的架构，以近乎人类的方式推理、学习和适应。

In addition, as LLMs increasingly interact with multimodal data (text, images, audio, etc.), multimodal fine-tuning techniques will become essential. These methods will enable LLMs to integrate and process information from various modalities, enhancing their ability to perform complex tasks that require understanding of diverse data types.

此外，随着 LLM 越来越多地与多模态数据（文本、图像、音频等）交互，多模态微调技术将变得必不可少。这些方法将让 LLM 整合和处理来自各模态的信息，增强其完成需要理解多样数据类型的复杂任务的能力。

— 原书第 263 页 —

RAGRAG

RAG models will continue to evolve, integrating retrieval-based components with generative models to enhance accuracy and relevance. These hybrid models will retrieve relevant information from large databases or knowledge sources and use it to generate more informed and contextually appropriate responses. Advances in real-time retrieval mechanisms will allow them to access and utilize up-to-date information dynamically so they can provide current and contextually relevant responses. This promises to improve RAG models' effectiveness in applications such as customer support, knowledge management, and content creation.

RAG 模型将持续演进，把基于检索的组件与生成模型结合，以提升准确性和相关性。这些混合模型将从大型数据库或知识源中检索相关信息，并用它生成更有依据、更贴合上下文的回答。实时检索机制的进步将让它们动态访问和利用最新信息，从而提供当前的、贴合上下文的回答。这有望提升 RAG 模型在客服、知识管理和内容创作等应用中的效果。

Future RAG systems will better integrate with knowledge graphs and external databases, enabling LLMs to leverage structured knowledge for more accurate, detailed, factually correct, and comprehensive responses—even to complex queries.

未来的 RAG 系统将更好地与知识图和外部数据库集成，让 LLM 利用结构化知识，即便是对复杂查询也能给出更准确、更详细、事实正确、更全面的回答。

Innovations in retrieval mechanisms will focus on improving efficiency and scalability (Gao et al. 2024). Techniques like approximate nearest neighbor search and indexing will be optimized to handle large-scale data and reduce latency in retrieval processes.

检索机制的创新将聚焦于提升效率和可扩展性（Gao 等 2024）。近似最近邻搜索和索引等技术将被优化，以处理大规模数据并降低检索过程中的延迟。

To conclude, sparse models and modular frameworks will make LLMs far more efficient, while memory-augmented models will bring persistence and depth to their understanding. The future of LLMs is not just one of bigger models but smarter ones—architectures that grow, learn, and reason, forming a new foundation for AI-driven innovation across every aspect of society.

总而言之，稀疏模型和模块化框架将让 LLM 效率大幅提升，而记忆增强模型将为其理解带来持久性和深度。LLM 的未来不只是更大的模型，而是更聪明的模型——能成长、学习、推理的架构，为社会方方面面的 AI 驱动创新奠定新基础。

The Future of LLMOpsLLMOps 的未来

I expect the coming decade to bring a lot of innovation to LLMOps, including the infrastructure layer that will be guided by that framework. One of the biggest contributions of any Ops framework is that it helps practitioners understand what tools they can build to automate and streamline best practices across the industry. For example, the biggest contribution of DevOps was the boom in cloud services infrastructures. For MLOps, it was data- and model-versioning tools. For LLMOps, I personally believe that the biggest booms will be in tools for resource optimization, evaluation, and multimodal data management.

我预计未来十年会给 LLMOps 带来大量创新，包括由该框架引导的基础设施层。任何 Ops 框架最大的贡献之一，是帮助从业者理解可以构建哪些工具来自动化并简化全行业的最佳实践。例如，DevOps 最大的贡献是云服务基础设施的蓬勃发展；对 MLOps 而言，是数据和模型版本化工具；对 LLMOps，我个人认为最大的爆发将出现在资源优化、评估和多模态数据管理工具上。

Advances in GPU TechnologyGPU 技术的进步

GPUs play a key role in LLMOps, and their evolution will continue to drive advancements in model performance and efficiency. Over the next decade, several emerging trends in GPU technology will significantly impact LLMOps.

GPU 在 LLMOps 中扮演关键角色，其演进将持续推动模型性能和效率的进步。未来十年，GPU 技术的若干新兴趋势将显著影响 LLMOps。

The future of GPUs will see the rise of highly specialized AI hardware designed specifically for the unique demands of LLM training and inference, as Figure 10-5

GPU 的未来将看到高度专用的 AI 硬件崛起，专为 LLM 训练和推理的独特需求设计，如图 10-5

— 原书第 264 页 —

illustrates. Companies like NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel are developing next-generation GPUs with enhanced architectures tailored for AI workloads. These include more GPU cores, increased memory bandwidth, and optimized tensor operations to accelerate model training and reduce latency during inference.

所示。NVIDIA、AMD、Intel 等公司正在开发为 AI 工作负载定制的增强架构下一代 GPU。这些包括更多 GPU 核心、更高内存带宽和优化的张量运算，以加速模型训练、降低推理期间的延迟。

As LLMs grow in size, the need for efficient multi-GPU and distributed training strategies will become more pronounced. Advances in distributed computing frameworks, such as NVIDIA's NVLink and AMD's Infinity Fabric, will enable more seamless scaling across multiple GPUs and nodes. This will improve training efficiency and reduce the time required to develop and deploy large-scale models.

随着 LLM 规模增大，对高效多 GPU 和分布式训练策略的需求将更加突出。NVIDIA NVLink 和 AMD Infinity Fabric 等分布式计算框架的进步，将实现跨多 GPU 和节点更无缝的扩缩。这将提升训练效率，缩短开发和部署大规模模型所需的时间。

With the increasing computational demands of LLMs, energy consumption is a critical concern. Future GPUs will focus on enhancing energy efficiency. Incorporating techniques like dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) and using advanced cooling solutions will mitigate their environmental impact and operational costs.

随着 LLM 计算需求不断增长，能耗成为关键问题。未来 GPU 将聚焦提升能效。引入动态电压频率调节（DVFS）等技术并使用先进散热方案，将减轻其环境影响和运维成本。

Finally, although still in its infancy, quantum computing presents potential opportunities for accelerating LLM operations. Quantum processors could complement traditional GPUs, offering exponential speedups for certain types of calculations. Researchers are exploring hybrid approaches that combine quantum and classical computing to tackle complex LLM tasks.

最后，尽管仍处于起步阶段，量子计算为加速 LLM 运维提供了潜在机遇。量子处理器可以补充传统 GPU，为某些类型的计算提供指数级加速。研究者正在探索结合量子计算与经典计算来处理复杂 LLM 任务的混合方式。

— 原书第 265 页 —

Data Management and Efficiency数据管理与效率

As you learned in Chapter 4, effective data management is critical for training and deploying LLMs. Since LLMs require vast amounts of high-quality data, there will be an increasing emphasis on data curation and quality control. We expect techniques for automated data cleaning, augmentation, and validation to become more sophisticated, ensuring that training datasets are diverse, accurate, and representative.

如你在第 4 章所学，有效的数据管理对训练和部署 LLM 至关重要。由于 LLM 需要海量高质量数据，数据整理和质量控制将越来越受重视。我们预计自动化数据清洗、增强和验证技术将变得更成熟，确保训练数据集多样、准确、有代表性。

Innovations in data storage and retrieval will be important for managing these massive datasets. Distributed file systems, object storage solutions, and high-performance databases will be incorporated into existing vector databases to handle the scale and complexity of data efficiently.

数据存储和检索方面的创新对管理这些海量数据集将很重要。分布式文件系统、对象存储方案和高性能数据库将被整合进现有向量数据库，以高效处理数据的规模和复杂度。

With growing awareness of data privacy, organizations will adopt advanced methods for protecting user data. Techniques like federated learning and differential privacy will be integrated into data management, allowing LLMs to learn from decentralized data sources without compromising individual privacy.

随着对数据隐私意识的增强，组织将采用先进方法保护用户数据。联邦学习和差分隐私等技术将被整合进数据管理，让 LLM 能从去中心化数据源学习而不损害个人隐私。

Synthetically generated data will become a key supplement to real-world data, improving training speed, reducing privacy concerns (as synthetic data is machine generated), and reducing reliance on expensive or scarce data. The Microsoft phi-4 small language model released in late 2024 has, by using some synthetic data, achieved good benchmarks at low cost and a small number of parameters.

合成生成的数据将成为真实数据的重要补充，提升训练速度、减少隐私顾虑（因为合成数据是机器生成的），并降低对昂贵或稀缺数据的依赖。微软 2024 年末发布的 phi-4 小语言模型，通过使用部分合成数据，以低成本和少量参数取得了不错的基准成绩。

Privacy and Security隐私与安全

Privacy and security will be paramount as LLMs become more integrated into sensitive and high-stakes applications. The deployment of LLMs will involve advanced security measures to protect against attacks and ensure data integrity. Techniques such as model watermarking, adversarial training, and secure multi-party computation will be employed to safeguard models from tampering and misuse.

随着 LLM 越来越多地融入敏感和高风险应用，隐私和安全将至关重要。LLM 的部署将涉及先进安全措施以防范攻击并确保数据完整性。模型水印、对抗训练和安全多方计算等技术将被用于保护模型免遭篡改和滥用。

As LLMs become more pervasive, ethical considerations will drive the development of guidelines and best practices for their use. New laws like the ones in the United States, the state of California, and the European Union will incentivize organizations to focus on transparency, fairness, and accountability, implementing measures to ensure that LLMs are used responsibly and ethically. Also, given the massive training and maintenance costs, it's economical for large AI providers to develop models that follow a large market's most restrictive set of rules and deploy them broadly, rather than train and maintain different models for each set of legal requirements. For example, if the EU requires that models only use anonymized data, it's economical to train and maintain one model worldwide that uses anonymized data rather than two, one that does and one that does not.

随着 LLM 日益普及，伦理考量将推动相关使用指南和最佳实践的发展。美国、加州和欧盟的新法律将激励组织聚焦透明、公平和问责，实施措施确保 LLM 被负责任、合乎伦理地使用。此外，鉴于训练和维护成本巨大，大型 AI 提供商开发遵循某一大市场最严格规则集的模型并广泛部署，比为每套法律要求训练和维护不同模型更经济。例如，如果欧盟要求模型只使用匿名化数据，那么在全球训练和维护一个使用匿名化数据的模型，比搞两个（一个用、一个不用）更经济。

— 原书第 266 页 —

Comprehensive Evaluation Frameworks综合评估框架

I expect that new evaluation frameworks will be developed to assess LLMs across a range of dimensions beyond standard metrics like recall and precision, including factual accuracy, logical accuracy, and coherence. These frameworks will incorporate both qualitative and quantitative measures to provide a holistic view of model performance.

我预计将开发新的评估框架，在召回率、精确率等标准指标之外，跨一系列维度评估 LLM，包括事实准确性、逻辑准确性和连贯性。这些框架将结合定性和定量测量，提供模型性能的整体视图。

Establishing industry benchmarks and standards, ideally from organizations such as the United Nations International Telecommunication Union (ITU), the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Standards Association (IEEE SA), and the International Organization for Standardization (ISO), will be essential for comparing LLM performance across different models and platforms. Standardized benchmarks will facilitate fair evaluation and enable organizations to make informed decisions when selecting or developing LLMs.

建立行业基准和标准——最好来自联合国国际电信联盟（ITU）、电气和电子工程师协会标准协会（IEEE SA）和国际标准化组织（ISO）等机构——对于跨不同模型和平台比较 LLM 性能至关重要。标准化基准将促进公平评估，让组织在选择或开发 LLM 时做出明智决策。

Ongoing monitoring and evaluation will become standard practice to ensure that LLMs maintain high performance over time. Techniques for continuous evaluation and performance tracking will help identify and address issues as they arise, ensuring that models remain effective and relevant.

持续监控和评估将成为标准实践，以确保 LLM 长期维持高性能。持续评估和性能跟踪技术将帮助在问题出现时识别并解决它们，确保模型保持有效和切题。

How to Succeed as an LLMOps Engineer如何成为一名成功的 LLMOps 工程师

To succeed as an LLMOps engineer, you need to take a system administrator approach to productionizing LLMs. As directly responsible individuals (DRIs), engineers must be able to understand, evaluate, and manage risk.

要成为成功的 LLMOps 工程师，你需要用系统管理员的思路把 LLM 投产。作为直接责任人（DRI），工程师必须能够理解、评估和管理风险。

Our LLMOps maturity model (Chapter 2) can come handy when budgeting for different kinds of errors, from software fault tolerance to model evaluation errors. You cannot monitor everything. Set reasonable expectations and automate labeling and debugging for different kinds of errors. These could mean keeping an error trail, creating groups of related errors, and using LLM agents to explain and even debug them.

我们的 LLMOps 成熟度模型（第 2 章）在为各类错误（从软件容错到模型评估错误）做预算时会派上用场。你不可能监控一切。设定合理预期，并为各类错误自动化标注和调试。这可能意味着保留错误轨迹、创建相关错误分组，并用 LLM 智能体来解释甚至调试它们。

An LLMOps engineer often acts as the on-call engineer, which requires dealing with all sorts of problems: hardware, data quality, privacy, and user errors. These issues need to be dealt with quickly, often as emergencies. LLMs can help LLMOps engineers sift through the problems and provide suggested solutions, increasing productivity.

LLMOps 工程师常常扮演值班工程师的角色，需要处理各种问题：硬件、数据质量、隐私和用户错误。这些问题必须快速处理，往往是紧急情况。LLM 可以帮助 LLMOps 工程师筛选问题并提供建议解决方案，提升生产力。

As you learned in Chapter 2, LLMOps has four goals: security, scalability, robustness, and reliability. It can be a tough balancing act to prioritize among monitoring inferences for security testing, optimizing the model inference pipeline, A/B testing the model releases, managing the compute nodes, and optimizing the run pipelines.

如你在第 2 章所学，LLMOps 有四个目标：安全、可扩展性、鲁棒性和可靠性。在为安全测试监控推理、优化模型推理流水线、对模型发布做 A/B 测试、管理计算节点和优化运行流水线之间排定优先级，可能是一项艰难的平衡。

— 原书第 267 页 —

Depending on the number of active users the LLM-based application has, the features under development, and the size of the team, LLMOps engineers' workloads can vary massively.

根据基于 LLM 的应用活跃用户数、在开发的功能以及团队规模，LLMOps 工程师的工作量可能千差万别。

Conclusion小结

The world of LLMOps is not just about cutting-edge technology; it's also about processes and measurements. Together, technology, measurements, and processes are the pillars supporting the future of AI.

LLMOps 的世界不只关于尖端技术；它还关于流程和度量。技术、度量和流程共同构成支撑 AI 未来的支柱。

In this book, you've learned about how to apply, deploy, and maintain LLMs efficiently. We discussed the importance of data quality and data management, and we explored the art and science of improving LLMs through fine-tuning and prompt engineering.

在本书中，你学习了如何高效地应用、部署和运维 LLM。我们讨论了数据质量和数据管理的重要性，探索了通过微调和提示工程改进 LLM 的艺术与科学。

We've examined the revolutionary potential of RAG to bridge the gap between the general knowledge possessed by LLMs and the recent and/or specialized data some applications need. We've also discussed privacy and security, recognizing that safeguarding our digital interactions is as important as advancing our technological frontiers.

我们考察了 RAG 的革命性潜力——弥合 LLM 所拥有的通用知识与某些应用所需的新近和/或专业数据之间的鸿沟。我们还讨论了隐私与安全，认识到保护我们的数字交互与拓展技术前沿同等重要。

Yet, amid these advancements, it's important to remember the essence of our pursuit. LLMOps is more than a technical discipline; it's about ensuring that our creations serve humanity in ways that are ethical, transparent, and equitable.

然而在这些进步之中，重要的是记住我们追求的本质。LLMOps 不只是一门技术学科；它关乎确保我们的创造以合乎伦理、透明、公平的方式服务人类。

Economists recognize AI as one of a very few general-purpose technologies, in the same class as the internet, electricity, or the printing press. These general-purpose technologies tend to be incorporated into almost every human activity, changing the trajectory of progress. LLMOps can help us make the most of AI, preventing and correcting problems and accelerating advances.

经济学家把 AI 视为极少数通用目的技术之一，与互联网、电力或印刷术同列。这些通用目的技术往往被融入几乎每一项人类活动，改变进步的轨迹。LLMOps 能帮助我们充分利用 AI，预防和纠正问题并加速进步。

The future is ours to shape. Let's make it a future that reflects our highest aspirations and our deepest values.

未来由我们塑造。让我们共同创造一个反映我们最高理想和最深价值的未来。
